question: Where does the camera live?
context: Mocks: Depth (2.5D) page, section The layers list and the camera. Either way there is one camera; without changes everything looks flat exactly as today.

options.label: Camera settings on the frame
options.summary: Click empty canvas and the panel shows the frame, with a Camera section: Perspective, Camera depth and Camera X and Y, each keyable. When the camera is keyed, a thin Camera row appears at the top of the timeline to hold its keys.
pros: No new kind of thing in the document
Perspective is where the frame's other settings are
Simple for the common case: set the perspective once and forget it
cons: Moving the camera is numbers and keys, not a drag on the canvas
The Camera row on the timeline is a special row, not a track
options.mitigation: Option B can be added later on top of this without changing anything people learned.

options.label: A camera you add, like Motion
options.summary: Layer, Add Camera puts a Camera track at the top of the timeline. Pick it and the canvas shows the frame the camera sees, which you drag to pan and push to dolly, with its settings in the panel. Without one, the camera stays still.
pros: Camera moves are direct manipulation on the canvas
What Apple Motion and After Effects users expect
cons: A new kind of layer to learn
The canvas has to show two frames at once: the camera's and the document's
options.mitigation: Only appears when someone adds a camera, so a person who never wants one never sees it.
